name: Melco Resorts & Entertainment
description: Melco builds and operates casino resorts in Asia and Europe: City of Dreams, Studio City and Altira in Macau, City of Dreams Manila, City of Dreams Mediterranean in Cyprus (plus three satellite casinos), a casino in Sri Lanka that opened in August 2025, and Mocha slot clubs in Macau. Casino gaming was 82.3% of 2025 operating revenue ($4.25 billion of $5.16 billion), with hotel rooms, food, beverage and entertainment making up the rest, and Macau alone produced about 86% of revenue ($4.43 billion). It operates under one of six Macau concessions (running January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2032) and is majority owned by Melco International Development (Hong Kong). It pays a lot of interest ($465 million in 2025), has not paid a dividend since suspending it in May 2020, and buys back stock.

hq.text: Hong Kong and Singapore, Hong Kong / Singapore (Cayman Islands incorporated)
hq.note: Principal executive offices: 38th Floor, The Centrium, 60 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong, and 71 Robinson Road, Singapore; registered office in Grand Cayman (FY2025 20-F Item 4)

employees.note: City of Dreams 8,515; Studio City 5,879; City of Dreams Manila 3,769; Cyprus 1,833; Other Operations (incl. Sri Lanka) 1,195; Altira 865; corporate 598; Mocha and Other 307 (FY2025 20-F Item 6.D)

businessLines.name: City of Dreams (Macau)
businessLines.how: High-end and rolling-chip players (often brought by licensed gaming promoters who earn commission on their volume) and mass-market gamblers lose a share of what they wager, which Melco books as casino revenue after Macau gaming tax, plus hotel, dining and show income.
businessLines.description: Premium integrated resort in Cotai opened June 2009: about 439 gaming tables and 635 gaming machines (2025 average); hotels Morpheus (about 783 rooms), Nüwa (286) and Grand Hyatt Macau (763); The Countdown being rebranded as about 150 luxury suites; House of Dancing Water show re-launched May 2025.

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Property EBITDA (segment profit); FY2024 $621.6M; FY2023 $576.3M. Margin computed by the scout.

businessLines.name: Studio City (Macau)
businessLines.how: Mass-market gamblers (day-trippers and tourists) lose a share of table and slot wagers, which Melco books as casino revenue, alongside hotel rooms, retail rent and attractions income; Melco Resorts Macau runs the casino and is reimbursed for the cost under an agreement with the owner entity.
businessLines.description: Cinematically themed Cotai resort opened October 2015, focused on the mass market: about 253 tables and 775 gaming machines (2025 average); 2,493 hotel rooms (Epic Tower, Star Tower, W Macau), a nine-screen cineplex, Ferris wheel, water park and 5,000-seat arena. Melco acquired 60% of the developer in 2011; the current stake was not read.

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Property EBITDA; FY2024 $341.2M; FY2023 $206.8M. Margin computed by the scout.

businessLines.name: Altira Macau
businessLines.how: Smaller premium-mass casino and five-star hotel; gaming win and hotel rooms, currently not covering its operating costs on the Adjusted Property EBITDA measure.
businessLines.description: Premium-mass hotel and casino on the Macau peninsula side: about 31 tables and 160 gaming machines (2025 average) and 216 hotel rooms.

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Property EBITDA loss; FY2024 $(1.9)M; FY2023 $(1.3)M

businessLines.name: Mocha and Other (Macau)
businessLines.how: Day-trip and local players lose a share of what they wager on slot machines in small clubs, with Macau law capping the total number of machines (12,000 market-wide) and requiring a managing company for premises Melco does not own.
businessLines.description: Non-casino slot-machine clubs (about 810 machines on average, excluding 160 at Altira) in leased premises, plus the Grand Dragon Casino until it closed in September 2025. Three clubs closed September-December 2025; three continue from January 1, 2026 under an approved management company.

businessLines.name: City of Dreams Manila (Philippines)
businessLines.how: Premium and mass players lose a share of table and slot wagers; revenue fell in 2025 on softer gaming and non-gaming results.
businessLines.description: Casino resort in Manila; Melco Resorts Leisure holds the exclusive right to manage, operate and control it. Melco raised its stake in the operator MRP to approximately 97.9% in December 2018 (MRP was delisted from the Philippine Stock Exchange in June 2019); current stake not read.

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Property EBITDA; FY2024 $181.1M; FY2023 $205.5M. Margin computed by the scout.

businessLines.name: City of Dreams Mediterranean and Other (Cyprus)
businessLines.how: Tourists and locals gamble in the only licensed casino group in Cyprus (exclusive until 2032) and pay for hotel rooms and dining; revenue grew 28% in 2025.
businessLines.description: City of Dreams Mediterranean in Limassol plus three satellite casinos in Nicosia, Ayia Napa and Paphos; Melco owns 75% (acquired July 2019) and holds the exclusive license to operate casinos in the Republic of Cyprus until 2032.

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Property EBITDA; FY2024 $50.5M; FY2023 $27.5M. Margin computed by the scout.

businessLines.name: Other Operations (Sri Lanka)
businessLines.how: Casino win from a new Colombo casino plus a management fee for running the Nüwa hotel; at start-up, not yet profitable.
businessLines.description: City of Dreams Sri Lanka casino (opened August 1, 2025) and management of the Nüwa hotel there (opened July 15, 2025).

operatingProfit.note: Adjusted Property EBITDA loss in its start-up months
